summary: Old Baldy: North Carolina's oldest standing lighthouse, an 1817 brick tower on Bald Head Island at the Cape Fear mouth. Decommissioned in 1935; now a climbable tower run by a foundation.

light.characteristic: fixed white (to 1883); red flash every 30 s (Mar 1883 to Mar 1893); white flash every 30 s (Mar 1893 to 1903); fixed white, fourth order (1903 to 1935) (LighthouseFriends)

staffing.note: Radio beacon in the tower 1941 to 1958 (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: Reached by a people-only ferry from Southport; climbing costs a fee; call ahead for hours (Town of Bald Head Island).

corrections.why: The Town gives 109 ft 10 3/4 in and the Foundation 110 ft, both about 33.5 m. LighthouseFriends says ninety feet. The record's 31.0 m matches none of them.
The marker, the Foundation and LighthouseFriends all give completion in 1817, and no source read gives a second tower in 1818.

corrections.proposed: red flash 30 s only from March 1883 to March 1893; white flash 30 s from March 1893; fixed white from 1903
corrections.why: LighthouseFriends and the Board's 1893 report both describe the change from red to white in 1893, so the record's red characteristic is only correct for 1883-1893.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The marker gives 1835 for discontinuance, but the Board's reports of 1891-1893 describe Bald Head as a working rear beacon, which contradicts that date. LighthouseFriends gives 1866 (when Federal Point was built), a return to service in 1879 and decommissioning in 1935. The Society gives 1930. The story gives the 1935 date and notes the others.
The marker (finished the following year after 1816), the Foundation (1 April 1817) and LighthouseFriends all give 1817; the record's 1818 event has no source.

LighthouseFriends says the replica beside the tower reproduces the 1850s keepers' cottage, finished in 2000. The Town says the museum replicates the two-story cottage built in 1883 on the same spot, lost to fire in 1931. The story states the disagreement.

resolved_conflicts.field: Frying Pan Shoals length and first keeper
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Town gives the shoals as extending over 20 miles; LighthouseFriends gives twenty-eight miles. The Foundation calls Sedgwick Springs the first official keeper of the 1817 tower; LighthouseFriends and the Society name Henry Long as the first keeper (1795-1806). The story gives both versions and attributes each.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) first lighting: 1794 (LighthouseFriends, marker), 1795 (Town), 1796 (Bulletin 1939); the story says the sources differ. (2) Tower height: 109 ft 10 3/4 in (Town), 110 ft (Foundation), ninety feet (LighthouseFriends); the facts field uses 33.5 m. (3) Original lens: 1851 (Society record) vs 1855 (LighthouseFriends); the Foundation says a third-order lens was installed to brighten the light, without a date. (4) Discontinuance: see resolved_conflicts; the Society's record also says 'Active Aid to Navigation: No' and 'Current Optic: REMOVED'. (5) The NRHP nomination (75001242) is a 'not digitised' placeholder in the cache; the 1975 listing date is from the marker entry (and matches Wikipedia's April 28, 1975, which is not cited). (6) The Board's reports of 1891-1901 call the light 'Cape Fear light (Bald Head)'; the 1903 Cape Fear Lighthouse on the island's southeast end is a separate station (us-nc-cape-fear). The story keeps them apart. (7) The 1913 Bulletin lists Bald Head among lights changed from fixed to occulting (OCR damaged, 'Bald Head, Cape Fear River' with 'fixed to occulting'); the Commissioner's 1915 section describes an oil-to-acetylene change. Not used; check the page image. (8) The Foundation says the lantern and third-order lens were removed during the Civil War and that their whereabouts are unknown; LighthouseFriends does not say this; not used. (9) Henry Long's death (1806) and the 1806 petition text are LighthouseFriends's account; the petition was not checked against an archive copy. (10) Town and LighthouseFriends disagree on which cottage the replica reproduces (the Town says the 1883 two-story cottage; LighthouseFriends says the 1850s cottage); not reconciled. (11) The 1851 'comparatively useless' finding is LighthouseFriends's quotation; the Foundation dates it 1852; the Board's 1851 report is not in the local corpus. (12) Chronicling America: no NC hits for a 1886 Bald Head earthquake report; the 'Dosher' hits (Wilmington 1901, 1904, 1907; Raleigh 1903) are unrelated people. (13) The Frying Pan Shoals lightship (1854) is a separate station; not told here. (14) The 1921 tender Cypress event is on the shoal, not at the light; cited only to show that no wreck is tied to the tower. (15) Keepers: all 14 roster lines are principal keepers; the person slugs come from roster.py. Springs's birth year 1756 is from the Society (LighthouseFriends's 80-year-old in 1836 agrees). Fact-check 2026-10-27: (a) The 1939 Bulletin's 1796 is an OCR line in a list of early lights ('Cap.e Fear Ri,el', N. C., 1796'); the story attributes it as the Bulletin's date, not as a verified first lighting. (b) The 1921 steamer event is in the Commissioner's 1921 section (scan p. 662, with the towing on p. 666); the Cypress's role is read from the same section. (c) Hunter is called a visitor, not an inspector: LighthouseFriends says only that he visited and reported. (d) The 1883 jetty and the 1851 'comparatively useless' finding are LighthouseFriends' text (the Board's 1851 report is not in the local corpus). (e) Copyrighted sources (LighthouseFriends, Town, Foundation) are paraphrased; public-domain Board, Bulletin, Commissioner, petition and NRHP-era text stays in quotation marks. (f) The story no longer says the light 'did not help in storms' (not in the Board text).
